title: The Vale of Ash
intro: The barrow on the hill has opened, and a gray blight creeps down the vale. Crops fail. Roads empty. The village of Last Light holds on at the wood's edge. Someone must go up to the barrow and end this — the old verses or the king's own crown are each said to be enough alone, no need to chase both. You walked in at dusk.

scout.name: Scout
scout.desc: quick and quiet; finds hidden ways

scholar.name: Scholar
scholar.desc: reads the old tongue; the scattered verses will come easy

envoy.name: Envoy
envoy.desc: words open doors that iron cannot

descs: Ash trees close in, gray on gray.

spots.name: The Split Oak
spots.desc: An oak split clean by old lightning right at the wood's edge. The village lanterns still show through the gap behind you. East and a little north, past the trunks, a broken tower breaks the skyline and a dull gleam of still water shows beneath it.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: You picture the wood as it lies: a loose square of trails around this oak. The village lanterns stay south, behind you. The tower and the drowned shrine lie east, the barrow trail runs north, and a hunter's camp lies west. Lost, just backtrack the way you came.

spots.name: Broken Bridge
spots.desc: A footbridge, half fallen into a dry streambed. The far rail is gone.

spots.name: Charcoal Ring
spots.desc: A ring of blackened stone. Someone camped here, and not recently.
onEnterOnce: Old ash, cold to the touch.

spots.name: Antler Stake
spots.desc: A stag's antlers, lashed to a stake at the trail's edge. A marker, not a kill.
onEnterOnce: Someone left this to be seen.

spots.name: The Ashfall Clearing
spots.desc: A wide clearing where the gray ash lies thickest, drifted like snow that never melts. East, the ground softens and black water glints between the trees. West, a thread of woodsmoke rises — someone's camp. A path also runs north.

spots.name: Camp Smoke
spots.desc: A thread of smoke shows through the trees. The hunter's lean-to stands just beyond, to the west.
onEnterOnce: Woodsmoke, this deep in the gray.

spots.name: Twin Stones
spots.desc: Two standing stones lean together, worn faces touching, like old friends caught mid-word.

spots.name: Sodden Verge
spots.desc: The ground turns soft and cold underfoot. Black water glints through the trees to the east, and something stone breaks its surface. A worn track climbs north toward the watchtower's shadow.
onEnterOnce: The wood ends in water just ahead.

spots.name: Gray Cairn
spots.desc: A cairn of flat stones, older than the wood. Travelers left charms here once.
onEnterOnce: Someone built this to be found.

spots.name: The Hollow Path
spots.desc: The ground dips into a sunken trail, walls of root and stone rising to either side. Through a gap in the trees to the east, the watchtower's broken crown breaks the skyline.

spots.name: Wolf Scrape
spots.desc: Claw marks score deep into an ash trunk, fresh enough to still weep sap.

spots.name: Tower Shadow
spots.desc: The watchtower's shadow falls long across the path here, even at midday. The tower itself stands just to the east, with a track dropping south to the black water below.

spots.name: Widow's Well
spots.desc: A stone well, dry and capped with a warped board. No one has drawn water here in years. East, the trees thin toward the barrow hill.

spots.name: The Last Trees
spots.desc: The ash wood thins to nothing here. Beyond, the hill rises bare toward the barrow.

spots.name: Herb Hollow
spots.desc: A sunken hollow out of the wind. Green things still grow here, just barely. West, the trees thin toward the barrow trail.

spots.name: Crow Perch
spots.desc: A blasted, leafless tree stands alone, hung with black feathers instead of leaves. The barrow trail lies west, past the thinning trees.

gate.name: Village Gate
gate.desc: The last gate before the wood. Lanterns burn all day here now. The square lies south; the Ashwood waits north.

actions.label: follow the worn trail north to the barrow
follow the trail east to the drowned shrine
follow the trail east to the old watchtower
follow the trail west to the hunter's camp

square.name: Last Light Square
square.desc: Packed earth and a dry well. The reeve stands watch by a notice board that hints at more than one way to end this. Inn west, forge east, chapel south.

actions.label: read the notice board
fx: Notice board: three old verses are said to lie in the drowned shrine and the old watchtower — both east through the ash wood — and in the barrow's own walls, spoken together at the throne to let the dead king sleep. Elsewhere: the reeve wants the barrow sealed, and the gray priest remembers the old king's grief. Old talk holds the elder's locked coffer keeps the king's own crown, taken from him long ago and the reason his rest won't come — hear his grief from him at the throne first, then press the elder for it, and setting the crown back in his hands works just as well as the verses. Either path ends it on its own — you need not walk both, though word is the two together leave nothing unresolved.

actions.label: follow the trail north to the barrow
follow the trail east to the drowned shrine
follow the trail east to the old watchtower
follow the trail west to the hunter's camp

inn.name: The Last Light Inn
inn.desc: A low fire, empty tables, and an innkeep glad of any face.

actions.label: rest by the fire
fx: You sleep without dreams and wake steadier.

forge.name: The Forge
forge.desc: Coals banked low. The smith works with the door open, watching the road. Iron and old smoke hang in the air.

chapel.name: Gray Chapel
chapel.desc: A small stone chapel. Candles against the dark. The priest wears ash on both hands. Wax and damp stone smell like the inside of a well. A door east leads to the elder's house.

elder_house.name: Elder's House
elder_house.desc: Ledgers, dust, and an iron coffer on the mantel. The elder receives you without a smile. The shutters are closed against the wood.

hunters_camp.name: Hunter's Camp
hunters_camp.desc: A lean-to and a smoke rack at the wood's west edge. The hunter watches the trees, not you.

actions.label: follow the trail south back to the village gate

drowned_chapel.name: Drowned Shrine
drowned_chapel.desc: Half a chapel, sunk to its windows in black water. A stone psalter stands above the waterline.

actions.label: follow the trail south back to the village gate
recall the water verse (scholar)
fx: The water verse comes back to you, line by line. Water Verse: obtained.

actions.label: work out the water verse
fx: The worn lines give up their meaning. Water Verse: obtained.
The water has taken too much. Slow going without a scholar's eye — not shut to one. Try again.

watchtower.name: Old Watchtower
watchtower.desc: An old watchtower, stairs still sound. Wind carvings ring the bell room at the top.

actions.label: follow the trail south back to the village gate
recall the wind verse (scholar)
fx: The wind verse comes back to you, whole. Wind Verse: obtained.

actions.label: work out the wind carvings
fx: The carvings give up their meaning. Wind Verse: obtained.
The lines blur. Slow going without a scholar's eye — not shut to one. Try again.

barrow_field.name: Barrow Field
barrow_field.desc: A bare hill and two stone doors set into it. The grass here is white, not gray.

north.lockedMsg: The stone doors are shut fast. Force might open them, ask the gray priest for a blessing, or search the hillside — roots and old rain may have hollowed a way in somewhere else.
north.hint: force the doors, get the priest's blessing, or search the hillside

onEnterOnce: So this is where the gray begins.

actions.label: follow the worn trail south back to the village gate
force the doors
fx: Stone grinds on stone. The doors open.
The doors do not move. Try again, ask the gray priest for a blessing, or search the hillside for another way in.

actions.label: force the doors
fx: Stone grinds on stone. The doors open.
The doors do not move. The priest won't help now, sworn as you are — brace and try again, or search the hillside for another way in.

actions.label: search for the keeper's crack (scout)
fx: A narrow gap behind the ivy. You work it wider.
Nothing yet. The hill keeps its secrets — force or a blessing could still open the doors outright.

actions.label: search the hillside for a hidden passage
fx: Roots and old rain have hollowed a gap beneath a fallen lintel stone. You squeeze through into the dark below.
The hillside holds its shape. Nothing gives way yet — force or a blessing could still open the doors outright.

antechamber.name: Barrow Antechamber
antechamber.desc: Cut stone, older than the village. Shelf niches stand empty, save for a heavy door to the east and a passage north, deeper into the barrow. Cold air moves up from below, and your breath shows in it.

vault.name: Vault
vault.desc: A side chamber the wight never had to guard — the old king trusted iron more than claws. A strongbox sits under years of dust, its lock long rusted.
onEnterOnce: Whatever this held, no one has touched it in a long time.

actions.label: force the strongbox
fx: The rusted lock snaps at last. Inside: a seal of office, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.
The lock holds, this time. Rusted iron, not sealed magic — keep at it and it will give.

actions.label: pick the strongbox's lock (scout)
fx: The old pins give way, one by one. Inside: a seal of office, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.
Not yet, but the pins are turning. Keep working the lock and it will open.

actions.label: read the king's writing
fx: "Forty years I kept faith. It was my own blood who lifted the crown from my sleeping brow and called it inheritance. I do not want the vale to suffer for his theft. I only wanted to be believed."

hall_of_verses.name: Hall of Verses
hall_of_verses.desc: Every wall is cut with lines of old writing. Some of it almost reads itself.

up.lockedMsg: There is a stair here somewhere. The walls say where.
up.hint: read the stone verse on these walls first

actions.label: study the stone walls (scholar)
fx: The stone verse reads itself to you: a stair is cut into the wall right here, leading up. Stone Verse: obtained.

actions.label: work out the stone verse
fx: The verse comes clear: a stair is cut into the wall right here, leading up. Stone Verse: obtained.
The old letters swim. Slow going without a scholar's eye — not shut to one. Try again.

crypt.name: Crypt
crypt.desc: Low vaults and stone boxes. Something stands between you and the north passage. Old halls like this rarely have only one door.

north.lockedMsg: The wight bars the way north.
north.hint: defeat or slip past the wight first

actions.label: slip past the wight (scout)
fx: You keep to the shadow and slip by.
Claws rake you as you dart back. Quiet hands can try again — or stand and fight it here.

throne.name: Throne of the Barrow
throne.desc: The Hollow King sits on a stone seat. Where a crown should be, there is nothing. The air is very still.
onEnterOnce: So this is where it ends. Whatever you choose here decides how.

actions.label: speak the three verses at the throne
fx: You speak the three verses. The king closes his eyes like a man finally allowed to sleep. The gray lifts from the vale by morning. The barrow doors stand open behind you — you made the reeve no promise to shut them.

actions.label: speak the three verses at the throne
fx: You speak the three verses. The king closes his eyes like a man finally allowed to sleep. The gray lifts from the vale by morning. True to your word, the barrow doors seal shut behind you for good.

actions.label: the stone verse is still unspoken
fx: It waits down these stairs, cut into the Hall of Verses.

actions.label: the water verse is still unspoken
fx: It waits in the drowned shrine, east of the wood.

actions.label: the wind verse is still unspoken
fx: It waits atop the old watchtower.

actions.label: return the crown
fx: You set the crown in his hands. He stands, bows once, and lies down at last. The gray goes out of the trees like a tide. The barrow doors stand open behind you — you made the reeve no promise to shut them.

actions.label: return the crown
fx: You set the crown in his hands. He stands, bows once, and lies down at last. The gray goes out of the trees like a tide. True to your word, the barrow doors seal shut behind you for good.

actions.label: return the crown and speak the three verses
fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him, all at once. He listens through them with the crown finally where it belongs, and something in his face settles the rest of the way. The gray lifts from the vale by morning and does not come back. The barrow doors stand open behind you — you made the reeve no promise to shut them.

actions.label: return the crown and speak the three verses
fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him, all at once. He listens through them with the crown finally where it belongs, and something in his face settles the rest of the way. The gray lifts from the vale by morning and does not come back. True to your word, the barrow doors seal shut behind you for good.

actions.label: kneel and become the vale's new hollow king
fx: You kneel. The crown of nothing settles on you, light as ash. The vale will have a king after all — and no dawn. No one promised to seal this place; now no one needs to.

actions.label: kneel and become the vale's new hollow king
fx: You kneel. The crown of nothing settles on you, light as ash. The vale will have a king after all — and no dawn. The seal you promised the reeve no longer matters — you are what the doors would have kept in.

mail_shirt.name: mail shirt
mail_shirt.hint: Worn armor; the best you carry protects you.

river_charm.name: river charm
river_charm.hint: A ward against harm, worn like armor.

fx: Bitter, but they ease the ache. You feel a little steadier (+3 hp).

topics.label: the blight
topics.say: It kills slow. Crops first, then cattle, then the will to stay. It started the night the barrow opened.

topics.label: the barrow
topics.say: Seal it. Whatever is down there, promise me you'll seal it under stone and the watch stands with you. Mind — the gray priest keeps his own counsel on this. Promise us both and you'll have promised neither.

topics.label: promise to seal the barrow
topics.say: Good. The watch stands with you now.

topics.label: the watch's aid
topics.say: Then take the watch shield. It has stopped worse than claws.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say. One in the drowned shrine east of the wood, one up the old watchtower north of that, one cut into the barrow stone itself. And the hunter at the west edge trades herbs. A scholar's eye reads them quick — anyone else will have to puzzle them out slow, and it may take a few tries.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — one in the drowned shrine, one up the old watchtower, one cut into the barrow stone, slow going without a scholar's eye. Word is the elder holds something taken from the old king himself; a silver tongue might settle that debt quicker than any verse. The hunter west trades herbs.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — one in the drowned shrine, one up the old watchtower, one cut into the barrow stone, slow going without a scholar's eye. But quiet hands find their own ways in where doors won't open. The hunter west trades herbs.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — one in the drowned shrine, one up the old watchtower, one cut into the barrow stone, slow going without a scholar's eye. Whatever's down there, plenty would rather you just settle it with steel. The hunter west trades herbs.

topics.label: the old king
topics.say: He was a good king, long ago, and he was robbed in his grave. Grief like that does not lie quiet. Ask me for a blessing and I will open the barrow doors myself — no strength needed.

topics.label: the old king
topics.say: He was a good king, long ago, and he was robbed in his grave. Grief like that does not lie quiet. You have already given the reeve your word, though — I will not offer what undoes it. The doors must open some other way now.

topics.label: a blessing for the barrow
topics.say: Go with the gray blessing, then. Far off on the hill, the stone doors glow faintly and creak open — go whenever you're ready.

topics.label: steel for the barrow
topics.say: Take the plain sword — and hold still, I'll put a working edge on whatever you carry.

topics.label: the vale
topics.say: Four hundred years this village has kept the wood's edge. It will not end on my page of the ledger.

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: You ask about the coffer. The elder's hand covers the ledger. "That's not open to asking — not from you, not yet. Go hear what the dead king himself grieves over, up in the barrow, and come back with a better reason."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: No lock holds this shut, only the elder's own doubt. You press the old king's grievance on them, your word against their will, and the elder's hands close on the ledger.
fx: Your words find the old argument the elder has been having with themself, and settle it. The coffer creaks open. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size.

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: No lock holds this shut, only the elder's own doubt. You press the old king's grievance on them, your word against their will, and the elder's hands close on the ledger.
fx: At last your will outlasts the elder's. Their hands unclench, and they open the coffer. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size.
The elder's resolve holds, this time. Ask again, the same question, and press harder — the coffer will give eventually. Or leave it: the barrow verses reach the same end without the crown.

topics.label: the wood
topics.say: Wolves gone gray and wrong. Keep moving and keep iron close.

topics.label: trade for herbs
topics.say: Take them. Pay me by ending this.

ash_wolf.name: ash wolf
onDeath: The wolf drops. Its gray coat goes to dust.

barrow_wight.name: barrow-wight
onDeath: The wight comes apart into rag and bone.

hollow_king.name: hollow king

topics.label: why do you linger
topics.say: My crown. The first reeve took it from my barrow, and my rest went with it — the elder keeps it sealed away now. Bring it back, or speak the old verses here if you know them — either will let me rest. Or finish what the thief began.

topics.label: the blight
topics.say: It is my grief, spilled over the land. It will not stop while I wake.

onDeath: The king breaks apart into dust and old iron. The blight dies with him. The vale will not know why, only that the light came back.
